answer: A farm running 182 keys therefore forfeits that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation cheap. Because the river stake is held until the ledge settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the yarrow audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 49% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a cheap one. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
